speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two-and-twenty miles since four this morning, and the left heel has an opinion.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Barley. All this side of Aylesbury. It should be to a man's belt by now and it's to his knee. Nobody says anything. They look up and they look down and they go on reaping what there is.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She'll ask why I walked. I'll say the horse was dear. It was dear. …It's not why.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I wanted to be tired when I got there. I wanted to have paid something.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Now. The boy. Under the wall. He's come over the wall, he's in the dark, and she's above, and she doesn't know he's there. So she can say it. She can say the thing nobody says when they know they're heard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That's the whole of it. She thinks she's alone.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And he mustn't answer too soon. If he answers too soon it's a wooing. If he waits it's… he's overhearing a soul. Let him wait. Let him stand in the dark and be afraid to breathe.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: What's in a name. What's… a name. Something with a flower. Any flower. …No, not any.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I shall lose this before Grendon. Say it again tonight. Wall. Dark. She thinks she's alone. He waits.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: …There's a church tower. Is that Waddesdon? God send it's Waddesdon and they have ale.
